subject: StrikeForce escalation: LyricPay throughput degradation & exec liaison
messages:
From: Michael Chen <michael.chen@lyricpay.com>
To: jasmine.liu@redwood.com
Cc: support@lyricpay.com
Date: Tue, 30 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production alert: LyricPay throughput drop, 5xx spike

Hi Jasmine —

We started seeing a sharp throughput drop on our Redwood routes at ~08:45 PDT. Key observations:
- Our request throughput is down ~40% vs baseline.
- 5xx error rate spiked to ~12% over the last 20 minutes.
- P95 latency jumped from ~220ms to ~1.6s.

This is impacting checkout flows for some merchants. Attaching a short sample of recent error traces and the spike graph. Please escalate — we need an immediate mitigation and an ETA for full restoration.

We’re available now for a call. Michael Chen (CTO)
LyricPay

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
To: jasmine.liu@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com
Cc: Michael Chen <michael.chen@lyricpay.com>
Date: Tue, 30 May 2028 09:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production alert: LyricPay throughput drop, 5xx spike

On Tue, May 30, 2028 at 09:12 AM Michael Chen <michael.chen@lyricpay.com> wrote:
> We started seeing a sharp throughput drop on our Redwood routes at ~08:45 PDT...

Quick initial triage notes (live from the war-room):
- Telemetry shows a sudden increase in KV-cache miss rate for sessions tied to LyricPay’s primary model variant (variant-v3). Miss rate jumped ~6x at 08:41.
- Memory pressure observed on two serving pods (gpu-serve-07/08) leading to elevated GC pauses and tokenization latency.
- Error traces in prod point to transient OOM/retry loops in the attention kernel for long-sequence inputs. Sample snippets attached.

Immediate mitigations I recommend now:
A) Route LyricPay traffic to variant-v3-compact (smaller memory footprint, identical logits for our test prompts) — this reduces memory pressure.
B) Reduce max-batch-size from 64 -> 32 for LyricPay until we stabilize.
C) Evict long-lived prefix cache entries for sessions with >10k tokens to free KV cache.

I’ll apply A/B for a small slice (5%) first and monitor. If error rate drops in 10 minutes, we pull to 100%.

Attachments: prod_error_snippets.txt

— Karthik Iyer
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

From: jasmine.liu@redwood.com

Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com, lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 30 May 2028 15:02:00 -07:00
Subject: StrikeForce update: mitigation applied, monitoring, next steps

Michael — quick update and summary for your teams.

What we observed: throughput down ~40%, 5xx spike to ~12%, P95 latency ~1.6s.
What we did (completed):
- Deployed variant-v3-compact to 100% of LyricPay traffic (rolled 5% -> 100% after successful check).
- Reduced max-batch-size for LyricPay to 32.
- Evicted long-lived prefix cache entries contributing to KV pressure.

Immediate effect: error rate reduced to 2.1% within 18 minutes of full roll, throughput recovered to ~92% of baseline, P95 improved to ~280ms. We are continuing to monitor for regression windows.

Next steps (owned):
- Karthik: follow-up root-cause RCA and kernel-level analysis; estimated draft RCA in 48 hours. (Jira: RINF-1298)
- Monica: Customer-facing post-incident email + credit paperwork; send within 3 business days.
- Lauren: Execs will get daily updates until we close the incident.

Attachments: latency_graphs_20280530.png, prod_error_snippets.txt, lyricpay-action-plan-draft.docx
Related links: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RINF-1298

We will provide a 1-hour follow-up if anything changes. Otherwise, expect the RCA draft and the merchant comms cadence as noted. Apologies again for the disruption — we’ll own the follow-through.

— Jasmine Liu
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
